name: Ensoniq ESQ-1
source: Ensoniq ESQ-1 Musician's Manual (1986, Rev. 2; software v2.0), https://www.synthmania.com/Ensoniq%20ESQ-1/Images/Ensoniq%20ESQ-1%20manual.pdf (scanned; read from the page images): MIDI page pp.20-24 (ENABLE states), waveforms pp.28-30, modulation sources pp.33-35, programming pages pp.42-70, WRITE pp.74-77, STORAGE/MIDI transfer pp.78-85, Appendix 1 (program numbers), Appendix 2 (MIDI implementation v2.0: header, dumps, requests, virtual keypad codes), Appendix 3 (MIDI parameter numbers), Appendix 4 (implementation chart), Appendix 6 (PCB structure). Cross-checked against: dsq1 (github.com/martinez/dsq1, ESQ/SQ-80 emulator: source/synthlib/ESQpatch.d, ESQdefs.d) and stuartkeith/esq1 (esq1.py) for the byte layout; SideQick (github.com/VincyZed/SideQick) for the request -> modify -> INTERNAL + dump + EXIT round trip and device inquiry; grapelanestudios/esq1-editor (hardware NRPN + keypad navigation notes); KnobKraft-orm adaptations/Ensoniqesq1.py; JSynthLib EnsoniqESQ1SingleDriver; Patch Base ESQ-1 help (overload/crash behaviour); Noah Vawter esqpcb.zip. Byte layout validated by decoding 84 real 40-program bank files (dsq1 resources/banks). Edisyn has no ESQ-1 editor.

ensoniq.channelNibble: Byte 3 = 0n, n = the ESQ-1's MIDI page CHAN (base channel) - 1. The ESQ-1 ignores SysEx whose n differs from its base channel, and ignores all SysEx unless MIDI page ENABLE = KEYS+CT+PC+SS+SX. Its own dumps carry its base channel.

formats.singleProgramDump: F0 0F 02 0n 01 <204 nybbles> F7 = 210 bytes. Transmitted: the straight-synth program (reply to 09, or STORAGE > MIDI SEND > CURRENT PROGRAM). Received: into the EDIT BUFFER, only while a Program Select page is showing; afterwards the ESQ-1 shows the WRITE PROGRAM page.
formats.allProgramDump: F0 0F 02 0n 02 <40 x 204 nybbles = 8160> F7 = 8166 bytes. The 40 INTERNAL programs in order (program i = bytes i*102..i*102+101 unpacked). Received: replaces all internal memory at once (Program Select page required).
formats.allProgramDumpRequest: F0 0F 02 0n 0A F7 -> all program dump (02) of internal memory.
formats.virtualKeypad: F0 0F 02 0n 0E <button codes...> F7. One byte per event: button DOWN code 01-33h, UP code = down + 33h (52-102). Always send the up for every down (a dangling down hangs the keypad processor). Code 00 and codes outside the table must never be sent.
formats.noChecksum: Program dumps carry no checksum and no program number.

ensoniq.nybbleOrder: low nybble first, then high: byte b -> [b & 0F, b >> 4]; each MIDI byte is 0000nnnn.
ensoniq.requestsAnswered: The ESQ-1 answers 09 and 0A over MIDI, so the edit buffer and all 40 internal programs can be read without touching the panel. Cartridge programs have no dump: select them by Program Change and request 09.
pcbMap: 6-45: ENV 1-4, 10 bytes each (base 6+10e): +0 L1, +1 L2, +2 L3 [signed, value x2]; +3 T1, +4 T2, +5 T3, +6 T4 [bits 0-5]; +7 LV [bits 2-7]; +8 T1V, +9 TK [bits 0-5]
46-57: LFO 1-3, 4 bytes each (base 46+4l): +0 [W1 W0 | FREQ 6]; +1 [M3 M2 | L1 6]; +2 [M1 M0 | L2 6]; +3 [RESET | HUMAN | DELAY 6]

58-87: OSC 1-3, 10 bytes each (base 58+10o): +0 pitch = (OCT+3)*12+SEMI [bits 0-6]; +1 FINE [bits 3-7]; +2 [FM SRC2 hi | FM SRC1 lo]; +3 FM AMT1, +4 FM AMT2 [signed, value x2]; +5 WAVE [byte]; +6 [DCA ENABLE | DCA LEVEL bits 1-6]; +7 [AM SRC2 hi | AM SRC1 lo]; +8 AM AMT1, +9 AM AMT2 [signed, value x2]
100: [PAN hi nybble | PAN MOD SRC lo nybble]

keypad.softkeyLayout: SOFTKEY 0-4 = the five buttons above the display, left to right; 5-9 = the five below (inferred; program slot k of a bank page = SOFTKEY k-1, *EXIT* on the WRITE page = SOFTKEY 5).

nrpn.select: CC98 (Param Select Low) = parameter & 7F, then CC99 (Param Select High) = parameter >> 7
nrpn.data: CC6 (Data Entry) 0-127 spread over the parameter's whole range; CC96 = increment, CC97 = decrement the selected parameter
nrpn.numbers: Appendix 3 parameter numbers 0-131 (program) and 132-147 (global, not modelled); per-param 'nrpn'
nrpn.receive: Only with ENABLE = KEYS+CT+PC+SS+SX. With lower ENABLE settings the ESQ-1 still transmits them.

ensoniq.deviceInquiry: OS 3.00 and later: F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 -> F0 7E <base ch> 06 02 0F 02 00 <model 01 = ESQ-1, 02 = ESQ-M/SQ-80M, 03 = SQ-80> 00 <2 bytes> <OS minor> <OS major> F7 (15 bytes; per SideQick). Older OS: no reply -- probe with 09 instead.

wavesNote: OSC waveform numbers 0-31 in panel (up-arrow) order, manual pp.28-30. Waves 32-74 are hidden ROM waves reachable by SysEx on OS 3.5x only.
modSourcesNote: 4-bit modulation source value 0-15 (LFO/DCA/filter/pan/pitch mods and LFO depth).

params.name: DCA 4 Env 4 Depth (final volume)
params.note: DCA 4 is always modulated by ENV 4; this is the depth. Bits 1-6.

params.name: AM (osc 1 modulates osc 2 amplitude)
params.note: Osc 2's DCA is then ignored. The OS will not run AM and SYNC together.

params.name: Filter Resonance (Q)
params.note: Bits 0-4. Values above 31 (bits 5-7) give self-oscillation on the hardware (SideQick) but are outside the panel range; not modelled -- keep bits 5-7 from the mirror.

params.name: Filter Mod 1 Depth
params.note: 7-bit two's complement in bits 0-6 (-63 = 41h); bit 7 is the VC mode flag.

params.name: VC -- Voice Restart
params.note: ON: a restruck key reuses (steals) its voice. Appendix 3/6 call this bit 'rotate'. Polarity inferred (see uncertain).

params.name: Filter Keyboard Tracking
params.note: 'FC MODAMT 3' in Appendix 6; bits 1-6 (stored x2). 63 = about 1 octave of cutoff per keyboard octave.

params.name: Split Key
params.note: MIDI key number 21-108 (middle C = 60; the ESQ-1 keyboard is 36-96). The split key itself plays the upper program. Many real dumps hold 0 here when split is off (reads clamp to 21; harmless while Split = OFF).

params.name: Split
params.note: Composite: S flag = bit 7 of byte 98, direction D = bit 7 of byte 96. OFF = S0 (D kept); LOWER = S1 D0; UPPER = S1 D1. UPPER/LOWER = where the SPLIT program plays.

params.name: Layer Program
params.note: Absolute program location 0-119 (INT 0-39, CART A 40-79, CART B 80-119) -- a pointer, not a copy.

params.name: Layer
params.note: Halves polyphony to 4 voices.

params.name: Split/Layer Program
params.note: Layered with the split program when Split/Layer is on (needs Split = LOWER or UPPER).

params.name: Pan
params.note: 0 = left, 8 = centre, 15 = right (high nybble).

params.name: Pan Mod Depth
params.note: 7-bit two's complement in bits 0-6; bit 7 is the CYC flag.

params.name: CYC -- Envelope Full Cycle
params.note: Envelopes run all stages on every keystroke, ignoring key-up.

groups.name: Filter (CEM3379 4-pole low-pass: cutoff, Q, keyboard, mods)
Modes (sync, AM, mono, glide, restart modes, full cycle)

banks.label: internal
banks.note: INT banks 1-4 x 10 = PC 0-39. Read by requesting all 40 (0A) and slicing prog*102. Stored by bank read-modify-write (02) or single dump + WRITE-page keypad chord (see driverNotes).

banks.label: cart a
banks.note: E2PROM cartridge first half (PC 40-79). No SysEx read: select by PC, then request the current program (09). Writing possible only through the panel/keypad WRITE page -- not enabled (a missing cartridge would redirect the write to INTERNAL).

programs.note: Program Change 0-119 on the base channel (needs ENABLE >= KEYS+CT+PROG CHNG). There is no bank select; master bank is implied by the program number (Appendix 1). With no cartridge inserted, CART A/B are unavailable.

backup.restore: Press INTERNAL (keypad 26 59) so a Program Select page is showing, then send the saved 8166-byte all-program dump unchanged; wait >= 3 s (the ESQ-1 shows *MIDI DATA BEING TRANSFERRED* ~2 s).
backup.notInSysex: Global settings (MASTER/MIDI/CONTROL pages) have no dump. Cartridge programs cannot be read or written by SysEx directly. Sequencer data uses a separate alert/accept protocol (03-08, 0B, 0C) not implemented here.

setup: Firmware: the power-up screen shows the OS. Everything here works on 2.x; OS 3.00+ also answers the universal device inquiry (auto-detects the channel). OS 3.5x adds hidden waves (not modelled).
[MIDI] > CHAN = the editor channel (the base channel; SysEx carries it and the ESQ-1 ignores SysEx on any other channel).

[MIDI] > ENABLE = KEYS+CT+PC+SS+SX (data slider all the way up). Without SX nothing SysEx or parameter-change is received; without PC program changes are ignored. It has been seen to fall back to a non-SX setting at power-up and after a 'system error' soft reset -- check it every session.
[MIDI] > MODE = OMNI, POLY or MULTI -- not MONO (in MONO the straight synth receives nothing).
[MIDI] > OVFL = OFF (overflow mode sends notes out instead of playing them).
Straight-synth mode: no sequencer track selected (Tracks Select page: unselect), sequencer stopped.

Leave the ESQ-1 on a Program Select page (press INTERNAL) and never on the WRITE, STORAGE or a *YES*/*NO* prompt page: program dumps are only received on a Program Select page, and a stuck WRITE page blocks everything (press *EXIT*).
No memory protect exists on the ESQ-1: internal writes go straight in. Save a bank backup first.
Cable both ways: interface out -> ESQ-1 MIDI IN, ESQ-1 MIDI OUT -> interface in (dump replies need the return path).
driverNotes: Ensoniq ESQ-1 (manufacturer 0Fh, product 02h). No checksums, no addresses, no program numbers in dumps. (1) FRAMING: every message is F0 0F 02 0n <type> ... F7 with n = channel() (the editor channel = the ESQ-1 base channel). Match incoming on F0 0F 02 xx <type>; adopt xx if it differs (the unit only ever sends on its base channel). (2) NYBBLES: a program is 102 bytes; on the wire each byte is two bytes, LOW nybble first: [b & 0F, b >> 4]; decode b = lo | (hi << 4). Single dump = F0 0F 02 0n 01 + 204 + F7 (210 bytes); all dump = F0 0F 02 0n 02 + 8160 + F7 (8166). Worked example (factory TRIBEL, channel 1): F0 0F 02 00 01 04 05 02 05 09 04 02 04 05 04 0C 04 ... -> 04 05 = 54h 'T', 02 05 = 52h 'R', 09 04 'I', 02 04 'B', 05 04 'E', 0C 04 'L'. Byte 46 arrives as 02 01 = 12h -> lfo1Wave = 12h >> 6 = 0 (TRI), lfo1Freq = 12h & 3F = 18. Byte 100 arrives 0F 08 = 8Fh -> pan = 8, panSrc = 15 (OFF). Byte 92 = 3Fh -> vc = 0, filterAmt1 = +63. (3) VALUES <-> BYTES (p.offset = byte in the unpacked 102): plain bits: raw = (byte >> bits.shift) & mask(width), value = raw; write byte = (byte & ~(mask << shift)) | ((value & mask) << shift). encoding 'signed': raw as above, value = raw >= 2^(width-1) ? raw - 2^width : raw; write raw = value & mask. (env levels and osc/DCA mod depths are width 7 at shift 1, so +63 -> 7Eh, -63 -> 82h; filter and pan mod depths are width 7 at shift 0, -63 -> 41h, keeping bit 7 = the mode flag). encoding 'pitchOct' / 'pitchSemi' (same byte, bits 0-6): pitch = byte & 7F; oct = floor(pitch / 12) - 3, semi = pitch % 12; write pitch = (oct + 3) * 12 + semi, clamp 0..96, keep bit 7. encoding 'fields' (LFO depth source): value = sum over p.fields of ((byte[f.offset] >> f.shift) & mask(f.width)) << f.at; write each field back into its byte. encoding 'splitMode': S = byte98 bit 7, D = byte96 bit 7; value = S ? (D ? 2 : 1) : 0; write: S = value > 0, and if value > 0 then D = (value == 2). ALWAYS edit a mirror of the last 102 bytes read (edit buffer or slot): several params share bytes and some bits are unmodelled but meaningful (LV bits 0-1, fine bits 0-2, Q bits 5-7, pitch bit 7, glide bit 6). (4) READ: requestPatch = send F0 0F 02 0n 09 F7, wait up to ~1000 ms for type 01 (SideQick uses 700 ms), decode -> mirror. It returns the program as currently edited (edit buffer). requestProgram(internal, p) = send F0 0F 02 0n 0A F7, wait up to ~5000 ms for type 02 (8166 bytes, ~2.6 s on the wire), slice bytes p*102..+101; cache the whole bank for a few seconds so a 40-slot name scan costs one request (requestSlotName = name bytes 0-5 of the cached slice). Cart banks: no dump -- programChange then requestPatch (the editor's 'loadable' path; it changes what is playing). (5) PROBE: send 09 and wait for 01 (900 ms). On failure, optionally F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 (OS 3.00+ answers F0 7E <ch> 06 02 0F 02 00 01 ...; take the channel from byte 2) or sweep n = 0..15 with 09 at ~200 ms each. No reply at all usually means ENABLE lacks SX. (6) KEYPAD: keypad(code) = F0 0F 02 0n 0E <code> <code + 33h> F7 (down then up in one message). Codes in ensoniq.keypad.downCodes; per-param p.page = the page button that shows that parameter (ENV1-4 01-04, LFO1-3 05-07, OSC1-3 08-0A, DCA1-3 0B-0D, DCA4 0E, FILTER 0F, MODES 10, SPLIT/LAYER 11). A hold chord is one message: <holdDown> <tapDown> <tapUp> <holdUp>. Track the page the ESQ-1 is on (unknown after connect, after any dump and after a Program Change). (7) sendPatch (edit buffer): the ESQ-1 only accepts a program dump on a Program Select page and then jumps to the WRITE PROGRAM page, where it accepts nothing else. So: keypad(INTERNAL 26h) -> wait ~150 ms -> single dump (01) built from the mirror -> wait ~250 ms -> keypad(SOFTKEY 5 = 2Fh, the *EXIT* button under 'EXIT' on the WRITE page; SideQick sends exactly F0 0F 02 0n 0E 2F 62 F7) -> the unit returns to the program select page with the new program sounding in the edit buffer. Leave >= 300 ms before the next dump. (SideQick sends INTERNAL as a bare down code 26 with no up; send 26 59.) Pressing INTERNAL only shows the bank page -- it does not select a program, so the edit buffer survives. (8) sendParam (live): two modes, keep the choice in prefs ('live' = 'nrpn' | 'dump'). NRPN mode (params with liveEdit 'nrpn'): if p.page != current page -> keypad(p.page), wait ~60 ms, mark the selected parameter unknown; then, unless p.nrpn is the last one selected, CC98 = p.nrpn & 7F, then CC99 = p.nrpn >> 7 (this order -- the only hardware report says MSB-first did not register), then CC6 = data. Do not use midi.nrpn(): it sends 99 before 98 and adds CC38. data = clamp(0,127, round((i + 0.5) * 128 / N - 0.5)) with i = value - p.min, N = p.max - p.min + 1 (bucket centre: correct whether the ESQ-1 scales by floor(cc6 * N / 128) or by rounding). Coalesce: while a message is queued keep only the newest value per param; one short message per >= 30 ms. Dump mode (and always for liveEdit 'dump' params: name chars, split/layer programs, splitMode): write the value into the mirror, then run (7) trailing-edge throttled to one dump per ~400 ms. Suggested: start in NRPN mode; after the first NRPN edit of a session, request 09 and compare the byte; if it did not change, switch to dump mode and tell the user. (9) programChange(bi, prog): C0|ch, prog + bank.select.offset (0-119). No bank select exists. It replaces the edit buffer; afterwards requestPatch (09) to adopt what is playing. Cart programs with no cartridge inserted are presumably ignored (verify: the reply to 09 will be unchanged). (10) writeProgram(internal, p, values): safest path (manual-documented, no keypad): requestProgram-style 0A read, replace slot p's 102 bytes with the mirror + values, keypad(INTERNAL), send the whole 8166-byte 02 dump, wait >= 3000 ms, then read back 0A to verify slot p (sameProgram). Fast path (single slot, relies on keypad): single dump (01) as in (7) but WITHOUT the EXIT press (the unit is now on WRITE PROGRAM), then one keypad message: 26 59 (INTERNAL, picks the master bank on the WRITE page) then <22h + bank> <2Ah + k> <2Ah + k + 33h> <22h + bank + 33h> where bank = floor(p / 10) (0-3 -> BANK 1-4) and k = p % 10 (softkey); the unit shows WRITING NEW PROGRAM ~2 s and returns to that bank's select page with the slot selected; wait 2500 ms, then verify with 0A. Return value = the 102 bytes written. Cart write: not enabled (flags false). (11) sameProgram(a, b): compare every modelled param decoded from the two 102-byte images (not raw bytes: LV bit 1, fine bits 0-2 etc. can differ harmlessly). (12) decode(ev): with ENABLE >= KEYS+CT the ESQ-1 transmits front-panel edits as parameter select CC99/CC98 + CC6 data (and CC96/CC97 for the arrow buttons) on its base channel. midi.js turns 98/99 + 6 into {type:'nrpn', param, value} with value = cc6 << 7 (no CC38): use cc6 = ev.value >> 7, i = floor(cc6 * N / 128), value = p.min + i, found by p.nrpn. Remember the last param for plain {type:'cc', num:96/97} (+1/-1). Numbers 132-147 are globals -- ignore. Also accept unsolicited type 01 dumps (MIDI SEND > CURRENT PROGRAM on the panel) as a full update. The transmit order of 98/99 is unverified; handle either. (13) PACING: gapMs 30 between short messages; never burst (Patch Base and the only other editor report the ESQ-1 crashing / soft-resetting with 'system error 03' -- which also drops SX enable -- under dense MIDI, e.g. a whole patch sent as parameter changes or a burst on load). Never send a patch as a stream of NRPNs; use (7). Wait ~150 ms after a keypad page press, ~250 ms after a single dump, >= 3000 ms after an all-program dump.
uncertain: LFO byte layout: Appendix 6 prints [M1 M0 | FREQ], [M3 M2 | L1], [W1 W0 | L2]. Real data says [W1 W0 | FREQ], [M3 M2 | L1], [M1 M0 | L2]: this is what dsq1 (jpcima/martinez emulator) and stuartkeith/esq1's code decode, and decoding 80+ real bank files with it gives LFO 1 = TRI + WHEEL with L1 = 0 on most factory sounds -- exactly the manual's own vibrato recipe (p.52) -- while the Appendix-6 reading gives NOISE + VEL2. Used the real-data layout. (stuartkeith's README table swaps the M bits relative to its own code; the code wins.) Vawter's pcb.c and the GrapeLane editor follow the (wrong) manual.

ENV parameter numbers: Appendix 3 lists ENV1 as L1 L2 L3 T1 LV T1V T2 T3 T4 TK (0-9) but ENV2-4 as L1 L2 L3 LV T1V T1 T2 T3 T4 TK. All four here use the ENV2-4 order, which matches the ENV page's softkey order and how every other page is numbered; ENV1 is probably a misprint. GrapeLane's editor uses the ENV1 order for all four. Test: on the ENV1 page, move LV and watch which CC98 the ESQ-1 transmits (3 or 4).

NRPN receive: the manual says Parameter Changes are received only with ENABLE=...+SX and gives only the numbers and 'Parameter Select controllers 98/99'. Everything else -- that the edit only lands while that parameter's page is on screen, that CC98 must precede CC99, that CC6 spans the whole range and that mod sources are 16 even buckets -- comes from one third-party editor tested on hardware (grapelanestudios/esq1-editor, 2026). Unverified here; driverNotes (8) includes a self-check and a dump fallback.

CC6 scaling for ranges other than those GrapeLane tested (wave, cutoff, mod source): the bucket-centre formula is safe for floor or round scaling, but params with odd spans (bipolar -63..63 = 127 steps, split key 21-108 = 88, octave) are untested. Program-reference params (126/128/130) and split direction (129: assumed OFF/LOWER/UPPER) are forced to dump mode because their data-slider range depends on cartridge presence.

Octave range: manual v2.0 says OCT -3..+3 and Appendix 6 says the semitone byte is 0..72, yet SEMI 0..11 at OCT +3 already reaches 83. GrapeLane (hardware) and SideQick (OS 3.x/SQ-80) both treat +5 (byte 96) as the normal top. Range set to -3..+5 (the ESQ-1 accepts out-of-range pitch bytes via SysEx anyway, per SideQick). For NRPN on OS 2.x the octave slider span would be 7 values, not 9 -- verify, or keep octave on dump mode for 2.x units.

VC polarity: Appendices 3 and 6 name this bit 'rotate'; the MODE page calls it VC (voice restart). Taken as bit 1 = VC ON, because factory pianos (PIANO1/PIANO2) have it set and pads (SLOSTR, SINPAD, MOODS) clear, matching the manual's advice (p.65). Verify on the MODE page after loading PIANO1.

Split direction polarity: D = 1 taken as UPPER (split program above the key) from factory pairs KICK/K+SIMS (KICK: D1, key 47, split program K+SIMS; K+SIMS: D0, key 37, split program KICK -- the kick sits on the lowest keys either way). Verify on the SPLIT/LAYER page.

Split/layer program values are taken as absolute locations 0-119 (INT 0-39, CART A 40-79, CART B 80-119): factory banks reference neighbouring internal slots 38/39 by those numbers and cartridge sounds by 40+. Not documented.

Current Program Dump Request (09): the manual says it dumps 'the currently selected program'; SideQick (hardware-tested) relies on it returning the program as currently edited. Treated as the edit buffer.

Program dumps received: manual p.85 says a single program lands in the edit buffer and the unit then shows the WRITE page; JSynthLib warns another dump is ignored until *EXIT* is pressed. *EXIT* = SOFTKEY 5 (2Fh) is inferred from the WRITE page drawing and from SideQick sending 0E 2F 62 after every dump; the softkey numbering (0-4 top, 5-9 bottom) is otherwise undocumented.

WRITE fast path: holding BANK n and pressing a softkey writes (manual p.76); doing it with virtual keypad events in one message follows the Appendix-2 rules but has not been seen working. Pressing INTERNAL on the WRITE page is assumed to switch the destination master bank (manual p.75) without leaving the page. Prefer the bank read-modify-write path until verified.
All Program Dump length: Appendix 2 prints '9160 nybble-ized MIDI bytes'; 102 x 40 x 2 = 8160 (8166 with header/F7), which is what real bank files contain.
ENV LV low bits: most real dumps store LV as value*4+2 (bit 1 set) rather than value*4. Meaning unknown (possibly written by some OS versions); decoded as bits 2-7 and bits 0-1 preserved.

Mod source order LFO1..OFF (0-15) and PRESS = 14: from dsq1 and the manual's listing order; GrapeLane hardware-confirmed ENV1 = 3 and VEL = 7 but its list omits PRESS. The manual counts '15 modulation sources' + OFF.
ENABLE persistence: the manual says settings are battery-backed; Patch Base and GrapeLane both report the unit coming up without SX (at power-on / after a soft reset). Setup says check every session.
Pacing numbers (30 ms per short message, 150/250/3000 ms waits) are empirical from GrapeLane/SideQick/Patch Base behaviour, not from Ensoniq.
Device inquiry reply layout is from SideQick's parser (model byte 01 = ESQ-1 for OS 3.00+); not in the v2.0 manual.

Cartridge: Program Change 40-119 with no cartridge inserted is presumably ignored; cartridge writes through the keypad would fall back to INTERNAL if the cartridge is missing, so cart banks are write:false.

Hidden values: waves 32-74 (OS 3.5x only), Q > 31 (self-oscillation) and pitch bit 7 ('low-frequency' range) are accepted by the hardware via SysEx (SideQick) but are outside the modelled ranges; the mirror keeps them if a patch already has them.
